title: Commercial Exterior Painting in Gainesville & Ocala
description: Commercial exterior painting for storefronts, shopping centers, and tilt-wall buildings: elastomeric and metal coatings, lifts, and phased traffic plans.
h1: Commercial Exterior Painting for Storefronts and Larger Buildings
heroIntro: Coating systems for tilt-wall, block, stucco, and metal, applied from lifts and scaffolding while your property stays open. Parking and entries are phased so customers can still get in.

sections.h2: A coating strategy, not just a color
body: Large commercial walls behave differently from houses. Tilt-wall panels and concrete block expand and contract with the seasons, and the joints and hairline cracks open and close with them. A standard acrylic can bridge those cracks for a season, then they show through again. Commercial exterior painting in Florida starts with picking a system that can handle that movement and the sun that comes with it.

For most masonry and tilt-wall buildings that means an elastomeric coating over properly treated cracks and joints. Stucco gets the same approach, with damaged areas repaired first through our stucco repair work. Where water intrusion is already a concern, our waterproofing and protective coatings can be added to the scope.

sections.h2: Surfaces we coat on commercial exteriors
body: Every surface on a commercial exterior gets the product made for it. Metal is the one most often done wrong: rolling wall paint onto a steel door or railing will peel within a season. Metal gets a direct-to-metal primer and finish instead.
bullets: Tilt-wall concrete panels and sealant joints
Hollow metal doors and frames, bollards, and railings
Metal awnings, canopies, and dock equipment

body: Commercial exteriors collect mildew, exhaust grime, and chalk from the old coating. Everything is washed first with methods suited to the surface; see our pressure washing and soft washing service. Cracks are routed and filled, failed sealant in panel joints is replaced, rust is cleaned and primed, and loose coating is scraped back to a sound edge. Two full coats is the baseline, and sprayed coatings are back-rolled where they need to work into block or texture.

Before any of that starts, we walk the building with your facility contact and photograph every elevation. Those photos document existing damage, such as impact marks, rust stains, and cracked sealant, so the proposal prices the actual repairs. They also give you a record of the building's condition before the work, which is useful for insurance and future budgeting.

Height drives a large part of the cost on a commercial exterior. Single-story storefronts can usually be reached from ladders and small lifts. Two- and three-story buildings, tall parapets, and warehouse walls need boom lifts or scaffolding, sized to the ground conditions and the space around the building. Landscaped islands, sloped lots, and overhead power lines all affect which equipment fits.

We assess access on the walkthrough and include it as its own line on the proposal, so you can see what the equipment costs relative to the paint. Lift work is sequenced so a machine is moved as few times as possible, which keeps the job shorter and limits how long any part of the lot is closed.
For buildings with warehouse or shop space behind the storefront, our warehouse and industrial painting page covers high-bay interiors, steel, and dock areas.

We plan the work around your traffic. Parking areas are split into sections and coned off in phases, lifts are positioned outside delivery windows, and storefront entries stay open with clean, clearly marked walk paths. In shopping centers, we schedule work in front of each tenant to avoid their busiest hours where possible.

Property managers get regular progress updates with photos so they can answer tenant questions without calling. Signage, door hardware, light fixtures, and storefront glass are masked rather than painted around freehand, and overspray is controlled with shrouds and by watching the wind, which matters in a parking lot full of customer cars. At the end of each day, cones and equipment are pulled back from entries so the lot works normally overnight. We are licensed, bonded, and fully insured, with workers' compensation on every crew member, and we provide a certificate of insurance naming your entity before we start.

sections.h2: Signage colors, graffiti, and long-term care
body: Brand colors on storefronts, accent bands, and logo walls are matched and recorded so future touch-ups do not drift. Buildings that attract tagging can get an anti-graffiti coating on lower walls, which makes cleanup faster and protects the new paint.

Our best exterior season runs from October through May. Summer work is scheduled earlier in the day, with crews watching the dew point and radar. Exterior work carries a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years on top of the manufacturer warranty. For the interior side of the building, see commercial interior painting, and for local details visit our Ocala commercial painting page.

faqs.q: What coating is best for a tilt-wall or block building in Florida?
faqs.a: Usually an elastomeric coating over properly treated cracks and joints. It flexes with seasonal movement instead of cracking. The exact product is named on the proposal.

faqs.q: Can you paint the outside of our building while we stay open?
faqs.a: Yes. Parking is closed in phases, lifts are positioned outside delivery windows, and entries stay open with marked walk paths.

faqs.q: Do you paint metal doors, railings, and awnings?
faqs.a: Yes. Metal gets a direct-to-metal primer and finish rather than wall paint, which keeps it from peeling and rusting through.

faqs.q: What warranty comes with commercial exterior painting?
faqs.a: A written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years on exterior work, on top of the manufacturer's product warranty.
